libya.title: Flag of the State of Libya

colors.note: Top stripe; represents the blood of those who fought for liberty and the Fezzan region.
Middle stripe with crescent and star; represents the dark era of Italian colonisation.
Bottom stripe; represents Islam, prosperity, and the Tripolitania region.
Crescent and star on the black stripe; symbols of Islam.

desc:
- Three horizontal stripes of red (top), black (middle, double-width), and green (bottom), with a white crescent and five-pointed star centred on the black stripe
- This flag was originally the flag of the Kingdom of Libya (1951–1969) and was readopted in 2011 during the civil war that overthrew the Gaddafi regime
- Under Gaddafi, from 1977 to 2011, Libya used a plain green flag — the only national flag in the world with a single colour and no design
- The three stripes represent the three historic regions of Libya: Tripolitania (green), Fezzan (red), and Cyrenaica (black)
- **Construction:** three horizontal stripes in ratio 1:2:1
- The crescent opens to the right (fly side)
- The five-pointed star sits between the cusps of the crescent
- Both are centred on the black band
- Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- From 1977 to 2011, Libya's flag was the only national flag in the world with just one colour and no design (plain green)
- Green represents Islam; the current flag returned to the tricolour after the 2011 revolution
- Libya has had more flag changes (5) in recent decades than most nations

desc: - During the Libyan Civil War, design without the star and crescent was common on homemade flags
- **Construction:** the Kingdom of Libya flag (red, black, green horizontal bands with crescent and star), revived during the 2011 civil war
trivia: - During the 2011 Libyan civil war, rebel forces readopted the pre-Gaddafi flag of the Kingdom of Libya
- The old tricolour became a symbol of opposition and was flown across Benghazi months before Tripoli fell

libya-jamahiriya.title: Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya
libya-jamahiriya.subtitle: Gaddafi regime

colors.note: Islam and the 'Green Revolution' ideology of Gaddafi.

desc:
- Under Gaddafi's Jamahiriya (1977–2011), the flag was a plain green rectangle — the only national flag
- in the world with just one colour and no design, insignia, or other detail
- **Construction:** a plain green field with no emblem — the only national flag in the world that was a single colour. Used from 1977 to 2011

countryData.name: Libya
countryData.officialName: Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya

trivia:
- The Libyan Jamahiriya flag (1977–2011) represented Gaddafi's unique political system
- The plain green colour represented Islamic socialism
- Replaced after Gaddafi's overthrow in 2011

libya-ar.title: Libyan Arab Republic
libya-ar.subtitle: Gaddafi era
desc:
- After Gaddafi's coup in 1969, Libya adopted the Arab Liberation Flag — a horizontal tricolour of
- red, white, and black — as part of the Federation of Arab Republics with Egypt and Syria
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and black with a hawk or eagle emblem centred on the white band
trivia:
- The Arab Republic of Libya flag was used during the Pan-Arab union period
- Represented Libya's role in Arab nationalism
- Changed during Libya's political transitions

libya-kingdom.title: Kingdom of Libya
libya-kingdom.subtitle: United Kingdom of Libya

colors.note: Fezzan region and the blood of the struggle.
Cyrenaica region; the dark era of colonialism.

desc:
- The flag of the Kingdom of Libya (1951–1969) featured three horizontal stripes of red, black (double width), and green, with a white crescent and star centred on the black stripe
- This flag represented the united kingdom formed from the three provinces of Cyrenaica (black), Fezzan (red), and Tripolitania (green)
- It was replaced by a plain green flag after Gaddafi's 1969 coup but was readopted by the rebel forces in 2011
- **Construction:** three horizontal bands in ratio 1:2:1 (red, black, green). A white crescent and five-pointed star centred on the black band. Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- The Kingdom of Libya (1951–1969) was an independent monarchy
- Overthrown in the 1969 revolution that brought Gaddafi to power
- The tricolour flag represented the short-lived kingdom

colors.note: The crescent and star of Islam.

desc:
- The Emirate of Cyrenaica (Arabic: إمارة برقة‎) came into existence when Sayyid Idris
- unilaterally proclaimed Cyrenaica an independent Senussi emirate on 1 March 1949,
- backed by the United Kingdom. Sayyid Idris proclaimed himself Emir of Cyrenaica at a
- 'national conference' in Benghazi
- **Construction:** a black field with a white crescent and star centred, representing the Senussi emirate
trivia: - Cyrenaica was home to the Senussi religious order, whose leader King Idris became Libya's first and only king
- The region's black flag with crescent and star became the basis for the Kingdom of Libya's flag

desc:
- After the Italo-Turkish War (1911–1912), Italy established the two colonies of
- **Italian Tripolitania** and **Cyrenaica**, which merged into **Italian Libya** in 1934
- They all used the flag of Italy
- **Construction:** the Italian tricolour used as the colonial flag for Italian Libya
trivia: - Italian colonisation of Libya (1911–1943) was one of the most brutal in African colonial history
- Italy's flag flew over Libya for 32 years, longer than many of Libya's own national flags have lasted

colors.note: The palm tree, representing agricultural prosperity.

desc:
- Tripolitanian Republic (Arabic: الجمهورية الطرابلسية‎, al-Jumhuriyat at-Trabulsiya), was an
- Arab republic that declared the independence of Tripolitania from Italian Libya after World War I
- **Construction:** a light blue field with a green palm tree and white star centred
trivia: - The Tripolitanian Republic (1918–1922) was one of the first attempts at self-governance in North Africa
- It was eventually defeated by Italian reconquest under Mussolini

libya-ottoman.subtitle: Tripoli
desc:
- The coastal region of what is today **Libya** was ruled by the Ottoman Empire
- - from 1551 to 1864, as the Eyalet of Tripolitania (Ottoman Turkish: ایالت طرابلس غرب‎ Eyālet-i Trâblus Gârb)
- - from 1864 to 1912, as the Vilayet of Tripolitania (Ottoman Turkish: ولايت طرابلس غرب‎ Vilâyet-i Trâblus Gârb)
- **Construction:** a red field with a white crescent and star, following Ottoman flag conventions
trivia: - Ottoman Libya used the standard Ottoman red flag with crescent and star
- The Ottomans controlled Libya for nearly 400 years (1551–1911) before losing it to Italy

libya-united.title: Flag of the United Kingdom of Libya
desc:
- The flag of the United Kingdom of Libya was identical to the later Kingdom of Libya flag — red, black, and green horizontal stripes with the Islamic crescent and star
- Used from independence in 1951, it symbolised the unification of Libya's three historic provinces under King Idris al-Senussi
- The wider black band honoured Cyrenaica, the king's home province
- **Construction:** three bands in ratio 1:2:1. White crescent and star on the central black band. Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- Libya briefly united with Egypt and Syria in various Pan-Arab unions
- The flags reflected Pan-Arab unity aspirations
- Unions were short-lived due to political differences
